scope: This fictional overview covers lateral ankle sprain as seen in professional basketball game video, for observational teaching only.

claims.text: This fictional overview covers lateral ankle sprain as seen in professional basketball game video, for observational teaching only.
The lateral ankle ligament complex stabilizes the ankle against inversion; a lateral ankle sprain is a stretch or tear of these ligaments.
Commonly observed non-diagnostic video patterns include inversion landings, landing on another player's foot, and contact landings.
Video cannot prove ligament grade, fracture, or syndesmotic involvement; only clinical examination and imaging can establish a diagnosis.
Diagnosis rests on clinical examination supplemented by imaging when indicated, not on video appearance.
Treatment is individualized and typically emphasizes early protected loading guided by clinical progress.
Return-to-play decisions use graded functional criteria at a high level; this overview does not reproduce any specific rehabilitation program.
